title: Threads API Pricing 2026: Free, but Rate-Limited
snippet:
Threads API pricing in 2026 is free. Meta publishes no paid tier, no per-call fee, and no pricing page in the official Threads developer docs.
**Is the Threads API free in 2026?** There is no dollar cost, but “free” hides two ceilings you plan around instead of a price. Production access waits on Meta App Review, and every call is metered by a 4,800-times-impressions rate formula with hard 24-hour publishing caps (250 posts, 1,000 replies, 100 deletions per profile).

| Threads API (Meta, official) | No paid tier or per-call fee published | Posting, replying, reading insights on your own account | Meta App Review for non-tester users, 60-day long-lived tokens, 500-char text cap |

The honest answer is that Meta has not published a paid tier or per-call fee for the Threads API, which is what most readers mean by “free.” The catch is that production access is still gated by Meta App Review and capped by a rate-limit formula tied to your account’s impression volume, which we walk through below.

### Official Threads API (no published paid tier)
The official Threads API surface lives entirely inside the Meta for Developers portal and has no published paid tier. You create a Meta app, add the Threads use case, request the permissions you need, and go through Meta App Review to take your app out of development mode.
The core scopes on Meta’s overview and get-started pages are `threads_basic`, `threads_content_publish`, `threads_read_replies`, `threads_manage_replies`, `threads_manage_insights`, `threads_delete`, and `threads_location_tagging`. Three more live on dedicated sub-pages: `threads_keyword_search`, `threads_manage_mentions`, and `threads_profile_discovery`. A newer `threads_share_to_instagram` scope was added on March 25, 2026, authorizing the `crossreshare_to_ig` and `crossreshare_to_ig_dark_mode` parameters on the publishing endpoint. Pull from whichever sub-page matches your use case.
Once your app is approved, it can act on any user who completes the OAuth flow, subject to the rate-limit formula below and the 24-hour caps. Meta’s public Threads API docs do not list a monthly subscription, a per-call charge, or a paid quota-increase product anywhere on the developer surface.

The API is included on every paid plan, with no per-post charges layered on top. The pricing page words it directly: “No per-post fees, no seat fees, no hidden tax on your soul.”

title: Threads API: Free Access, Posting Limits and App Review (2026)
snippet:
**Yes, the Threads API is free to use.** Meta's Threads documentation lists no price, per-call fee or paid tier. Posting to your own account needs a Meta app and no review. Posting for other people needs App Review, and each profile can publish 250 API posts per 24 hours.

Nothing in Meta's Threads documentation mentions a fee, a pricing page or a paid tier. I searched every page I read for pricing terms and found none. The real costs are indirect: somewhere to host media, and the time App Review takes if you need it.

### Is the Threads API free?
Yes, as far as Meta documents it. The Threads API pages list no price, per-call fee or paid tier, and you create the app in the standard Meta developer dashboard. The costs you can hit are your own hosting for media URLs and the time App Review takes. Checked on 4 Nov 2026.

title: Threads API Guide 2026: Post, Schedule & Limits
snippet:
**Short answer:** the Threads API is Meta’s official, free API for publishing to Threads and reading replies and insights. You need a Meta app with the Threads use case, a user token with `threads_basic` and `threads_content_publish`, and App Review before the public can connect. Posting is two calls: create a container, then publish it. There is no native scheduling.
## What the Threads API can and cannot do
Meta opened the Threads API to all developers in June 2024 ([launch post](https://developers.facebook.com/blog/post/2024/06/18/the-threads-api-is-finally-here/)) and has added features since. As of September 2026 the [official documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/threads) covers:
- **Publishing**: text, image, video and carousel posts, with link attachments, topic tags, polls, quote posts, GIFs from GIPHY, alt text, location tags and spoilers.
- **Replies**: posting replies (which is how you build a multi-post thread), reading replies, hiding them, controlling who can reply and approving replies before they show.
- **Insights**: views, likes, replies, reposts, quotes and shares per post, plus account-level metrics such as followers and demographics.
- **Keyword search**: public posts by keyword, once the permission is approved.

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Published posts | 250 per profile per 24 hours (moving window) |
| Replies | 1,000 per profile per 24 hours |
| Deletions | 100 per profile per 24 hours |
| API calls | 4,800 × the profile’s impressions per 24 hours (impressions counted as at least 10) |
| Text | 500 characters per post |
| Links | 5 per post |
| Carousel | 2 to 20 images or videos, counts as one post |
| Images | JPEG or PNG, up to 8 MB, 320 to 1440 px wide, sRGB, aspect ratio up to 10:1 |
| Video | MOV or MP4 (H264 or HEVC), up to 5 minutes and 1 GB, 23 to 60 fps, up to 100 Mbps; 9:16 recommended |
| Alt text | 1,000 characters |
| Unpublished container | Expires after 24 hours |
| Keyword search | 2,200 queries per user per 24 hours |

## Threads API pricing
Meta lists no fee and no paid tier for the Threads API. That is different from the [X API, which charges per post](/x-api-pricing/). The real costs are the ones above: App Review, the 60-day token refresh, the 250-post cap, and hosting your media somewhere public for Meta to fetch.

The Free plan is free forever with no card: 10 uploads a month and 2 profiles, with Threads, scheduling and API access included. Paid plans with unlimited uploads start at $24 a m

title: Threads API Guide: Everything Developers Need to Know (2026)
snippet:
Meta's Threads API gives developers free, full access to publishing, analytics, and reply management on the fastest-growing text platform. With 450M+ monthly users and zero API fees, it's the best opportunity in social since Twitter's early days.

Here's what you get access to:
- **Publishing** — create text, image, video, and carousel posts programmatically
- **Insights** — retrieve engagement metrics (likes, replies, reposts, quotes, views)
- **Reply Management** — read, hide, and respond to replies on your posts
- **User Profile** — fetch profile information and follower counts
- **Media Retrieval** — list all media objects for a user account
API Cost
$0
Post Limit / Day
500
API Calls / Hour
250

Rate limits on the Threads API are per-user and per-app. They're returned in response headers so you can track usage in real time.
| Limit Type | Threshold | Window |
|---|---|---|
| API calls per user | 250 requests | Per hour |
| API calls per app | 1,000 requests | Per hour |
| Publishing per user | 500 posts | Per 24 hours |
| Reply reads per user | 250 requests | Per hour |
| Insights per user | 250 requests | Per hour |
The rate limit headers you'll see in every response:

| Feature | Threads API | X (Twitter) API |
|---|---|---|
| Cost | **Free** | $100/mo (Basic) / $5,000/mo (Pro) |
| Post limit | 500/day per user | 1,500/month (Free) / 3,000/month (Basic) |
| Read access | Free, included | Paid tiers only (read was free until 2023) |
| Analytics | Free, per-post insights | $5,000/mo Pro tier |
| Auth method | OAuth 2.0 only | OAuth 1.0a + OAuth 2.0 + Bearer |
| Media types | Text, image, video, carousel | Text, image, video, polls, spaces |
| Search API | Not yet available | Available (paid tiers) |
| Streaming | Not yet available | Available ($5,000/mo Pro) |
| App review | Required (Meta review) | Not required |
The pricing gap is staggering. A [Threads AI tool](/blog/best-threads-ai-tools.html) developer gets full publishing and analytics access for free. The same features on X cost **$60,000/year**. For indie developers and startups, Threads is the only realistic option for building a social product without a significant API budget.

Is the Threads API free to use?
Yes. The Threads API is completely free for all developers. There are no paid tiers, no per-request fees, and no premium endpoints. This is a major advantage over the X (Twitter) API, which charges $100/month for basic access and $5,000/month for pro-level features.

title: Threads Has No Public API. Here's What You Can Still Get
snippet:
It is free, with no paid tier. According to [Blotato’s breakdown of Threads API pricing](https://www.blotato.com/blog/threads-api-pricing), Meta publishes no per-call fee, and the limits are per profile in a rolling 24 hours: about 250 posts, 1,000 replies, and 100 deletions.

### Is the Threads API free?
The official Meta Threads API is free, with no paid tier or per-call fee, but it is rate-limited per profile: about 250 posts, 1,000 replies, and 100 deletions in any rolling 24 hours. It is a publishing tool, so those limits are shaped around posting, not reading. A third-party read API charges per item returned instead, because it is doing the public-web reading Meta’s API does not.
